intent: A button inside the panel that closes its Drawer; the panel has no built-in close button, so this is its only close button.
typical_uses: A Cancel or Done action in the drawer's footer

dont_use_when.situation: A close action in an edge panel with no swipe gesture
A close action in a centered dialog

invariants.text: DrawerClose renders a native button with no kit class of its own; its look comes from `className` or from the element passed through `render`.
A press closes the Drawer whose root encloses it, reporting a close press as the reason to that root's `onOpenChange`, unless its own `onClick` calls `event.preventBaseUIHandler()`.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a non-button element through `render` while `nativeButton` stays at its default
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `nativeButton={false}` together with a `render` element that is not a native button, so the primitive adds the button role and keyboard handling itself

a11y.by: the primitive's Drawer.Close (Base UI's Dialog.Close) renders a native button; drawer.test.tsx asserts getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' }) on it and that clicking it removes the dialog ("closes via a consumer-composed DrawerClose")

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the close button's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the close button's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit sets no style of its own on this button.

good.title: A Cancel action stacked with the primary action

bad.title: A kit Button nested inside the close button
bad.why: DrawerClose already renders a native button, so this nests a button inside a button, which HTML does not allow; pass the Button through `render` instead.

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies.
